impact.rationale: The product change adjusts archive JSON token error classification and propagation; an incorrect merge could alter externally observed archive error codes, while the second changed file is test-only.

regressionLikelihood.rationale: The frozen test afterimage is byte-for-byte the non-overlapping union of the two previously reviewed leaves, and the frozen wire afterimage exactly equals the Primitive leaf; however, no Go compile or execution was performed in this review.

regressionProtection.rationale: Static byte, Git-blob, UTF-8, union, top-name, and skip checks passed. Prior leaf reviews cover the intended assertions, but exact-head Go tests and gofmt remain downstream gates.

recoverability.rationale: The freeze changes only two tracked Go source files and is bound to exact before and after hashes, so reverting those two files restores the analyzed base.

confidence.rationale: Confidence is high in the source composition and identity evidence, but only moderate in runtime safety because Go compilation, formatting, and execution were explicitly out of scope.

applicability.rationale: Both frozen before hashes exactly match the two Go blobs at e2829f8 and c648726, so the freeze applies to the stated base despite unrelated later non-Go history.

statusQuoRisk.rationale: Without the wire fix, decoder syntax errors can be collapsed with token-budget errors; without the strict-byte tests, claimed-original identity behavior lacks the accepted negative proof.

materialBoundaries.invariant: Token budget overflow remains CodeArchiveLimit while decoder syntax failure becomes CodeArchiveInvalid and is not collapsed by callers.
materialBoundaries.counterexample: A caller replaces any non-nil nextToken error with CodeArchiveInvalid, erasing the budget-limit classification.
materialBoundaries.legitimateControl: nextToken returns CodeArchiveLimit before decoder.Token, maps decoder.Token failure to CodeArchiveInvalid, and each object/array caller returns the received error before delimiter/type checks.
